newsitem.title: KENYA: 77 Kenyans killed or drowned after clashes.
newsitem.headline: 77 Kenyans killed or drowned after clashes.

text.p: At least 77 people were killed or drowned in the Kerio river in Kenya's Rift Valley after clan violence involving rustling, police reported on Tuesday.
Police spokesman Peter Kimanthi told the commercial Kenya Television Network that security officers shot dead seven cattle rustlers while up to 70 others drowned in a swollen river.

In its account, the Daily Nation newspaper reported on Tuesday that as many as 90 armed cattle rustlers were killed or drowned during a fierce two-day battle with security forces. Ethnic fighting often involves rustling.
The government said in a statement on Monday night that 19 people died in fighting between ethnic Pokots and Marakwets of Rift Valley province and that security had been beefed up.

Jackson Kalweo, minister of state at the presidency in charge of internal security, said the government was arranging reconciliation meetings and urged people to remain calm. His statement, read on state radio and television, made no mention of the drownings or killings by security forces.

Kalweo said the government did not want the violence politicised. In the run-up to Kenya's pluralist elections in 1994, at least 1,000 people were killed and 54,000 made homeless in ethnic violence, mainly in Rift Valley province, according to the U.N. Development Programme.
Kenya is due to hold general elections sometime this year.
The East African Standard reported that more than 400 Pokots and Marakwets have died in clan violence so far. It did not provide a time frame.

The Daily Nation said 100 cattle rustlers, believed to be from West Pokot in northwestern Kenya and on the border with Uganda, had been repulsed by a combined force of the paramilitary General Service Unit (GSU) and regular police.
"Many of the raiders were either shot or drowned as they escaped," the Daily Nation added in a front-page story.
In a separate incident, more than 40 villagers were feared drowned in floods in Kilifi, in Kenya's coastal region.
The East African Standard newspaper reported on Tuesday that the seasonal Kafuloni river burst its banks on Saturday night, flooding the village. It said many people were killed as they slept.
In a bloody start to the week in Kenya, 33 people were killed in a road accident on a motorway around Naivasha, 100 km (61 miles) northwest of the capital Nairobi, on Sunday.
